subject: Re: Invoice model surface — hosted vs Dedicated vs Private crosswalk (Integratech)
messages:
From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@integratech.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Integratech Procurement <procurement@integratech.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice model surface — hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (Integratech)

Hi Rishi / Lauren,

Thanks for the demo earlier. We had a follow-up from procurement and architecture to understand how your hosted baseline pricing maps to Dedicated and Private deployments. High level context: Integratech plans to onboard a chat assistant with ~1.2B tokens/month (expected steady-state) with predictable peak windows. Key asks from our side:

- Concrete hosted baseline (per-token) for your recommended model(s) for this workload
- How that baseline changes when we move to Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or Private (VPC on-prem) — what line items appear / disappear 
- Any one-time infra/onboarding fees, minimum commitments, and support SLA deltas
- Typical discounts for 12 / 24 month reserved commits and how they show up on the invoice

Procurement attached a short RFP. Can you provide a crosswalk matrix (hosted -> Dedicated -> Private) with invoice line examples (what we would see on a monthly invoice) and an initial range of commercial levers (commits, prepay, term, support). Also, do you have an example SOW for Dedicated to check onboarding milestones?

We'd prefer something we can share internally with finance/procurement in the next 48 hours.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Tran
Head of Platform Partnerships, Integratech
emily.tran@integratech.com

Attachments: Integratech_RFP.pdf (application/pdf)
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@integratech.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice model surface — hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (Integratech)

Emily — appreciate the clear ask and the RFP. Attaching a quick extract of the hosted baseline and a short narrative to help procurement map line items. High level summary below; full matrix attached (quick-ratecard-extract.csv).

Quick answers up front:
- Hosted baseline: per-token billing for generation + optional embedding/grounding calls. For your 1.2B token profile we'd recommend the Redwood-suggested open model (rwd-large) — hosted baseline: $0.0009 per generated token (est) for standard throughput.
- Dedicated: baseline token unit cost typically drops ~25–40% depending on commit and model-variant (we see 30% median for your size). But invoice moves from pure variable token lines to: reserved capacity (month), overage token line (variable), infra surcharge (GPU ops), and optional model license if using a gated variant.
- Private: larger upfront infra/onboarding fees + monthly platform fee for private control plane. Per-token variable price can be similar to Dedicated at scale, but the invoice will include infrastructure hosting (if we host), on-prem license, and optionally a managed services retainer.

Other line items that change between modes:
- Support SLA uplift (priority routing / 24x7) shows as a monthly addon
- Data residency / encrypted logging (compliance) can add a per-region storage surcharge or an annual compliance audit fee
- Egress / inter-region traffic appears on invoices for Private when cross-region replication is enabled

Commercial levers we typically offer:
- Term length (12/24 months): incremental discount ladder (12m: ~10–18%, 24m: ~18–30%)
- Commit level: higher reserved vCPU/GPU pools -> better unit economics
- Prepay vs monthly invoicing: 2–5% improvement for prepay
- Volume tiers and burst buffers: tiered pricing for sustained vs burst usage

I'll schedule a 30-min crosswalk call with our pricing ops and solutions eng to run through the matrix. Can you confirm procurement's preferred invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and if Integratech requires PO-specific line items (MSA/PO number on each invoice)?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Lead — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachments: quick-ratecard-extract.csv (text/csv)
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@integratech.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice model surface — hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (Integratech)

Emily — looping in finance (Marissa) and solutions (Ben) so we can provide a customer-ready crosswalk. Attached is a short draft SOW template that we've used for Dedicated onboarding and a one-sheet matrix in the Drive link we shared earlier. Highlights and an initial commercial position: 

- Hosted (what you'll see on invoice): 
  • "Generation - tokens" (variable) — per-token consumption charges
  • "Embeddings" (if used) — separate per-unit line
  • "Platform usage" (minor, e.g., API gateway)
  • Taxes/egress as applicable

- Dedicated (what changes):
  • "Reserved capacity" (monthly fixed) — covers baseline throughput + KV cache capacity
  • "Overage tokens" — variable beyond reserved throughput (higher per-token than hosted overage)
  • "Onboarding & infra setup" (one-time) — hardware prep, network peering, testing
  • Optional "Model license" for closed variants

- Private (what changes from Dedicated):
  • "Private deployment fee" (platform monthly + optional host fees)
  • "Managed services retainer" (monthly, optional)
  • "Audit/compliance" (annual or per-audit)

Suggested commercial concession for Integratech to get the PO over the line: 
- 24-month reserved commit on Dedicated with a 25% unit discount vs hosted baseline for committed volumes
- Waive up to $30k in onboarding fees if Integratech signs a 24-month commit and provides a minimum 50% prepay in year 1
- Standard net-45 billing; we can consider net-60 for enterprise finance approvals and a small fee (1.5%) for extended terms

I've attached draft-sow.docx for your review. If procurement confirms invoice cadence and PO requirements, we can generate a sample invoice and a one-page crosswalk you can hand to finance.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Invoice model surface — hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (Integratech)

Lauren / Rishi,

Thanks for the quick responses. A couple of clarifications from procurement: 

1) We need the MSA + sample invoice before we can put the PO on the schedule. Can you include a sample invoice with the "reserved capacity" line and the "overage tokens" breakdown?
2) Integratech typically requires no early-termination penalties for infrastructure that we co-manage. Is the onboarding fee refundable if we do not accept the Dedicated environment after testing?
3) Payment terms: our default is net-60 for enterprise vendors. We can consider net-45 if there is a prepay credit, but we need clarity on late fees and interest.

Please confirm — procurement will put this into the next vendor onboarding batch once we have the MSA + sample invoice.

Regards,
Integratech Procurement
procurement@integratech.com
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Emily Tran <emily.tran@integratech.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice model surface — hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (Integratech)

Team / Emily — quick internal approval and an update for procurement: 

- We can provide a sample invoice with reserved capacity + overage lines; Ben, please produce a month 1 / month 2 example showing the reserved commit consumption profile and a 10% burst overage scenario.
- On the onboarding fee refundability: we can make onboarding fees partially refundable (up to 50%) if the Dedicated environment fails to meet the agreed acceptance tests during the first 30 days. The remaining 50% covers third-party hardware & engineering mobilization. This is a customer-friendly concession to remove procurement friction.
- Payment terms: we will accept net-60 subject to a 3% early-pay discount if Integratech pays within 30 days. No interest beyond standard late-payment clauses in the MSA.
- Commercial concession for signature: one-time $25k credit against year-1 committed usage if Integratech signs a 24-month Dedicated commit and provides at least 40% prepay.

Next steps:
1) Ben — sample invoice and 1-pager crosswalk (drive link) by EOD Monday
2) Rishi / Lauren — share MSA + sample invoice to procurement once ready; loop in legal if Integratech asks to remove the initial acceptance holdback language
3) Emily / Procurement — confirm whether Integratech wants Redwood-hosted Private (we'll provide separate hosting costs) or on-prem private (you manage infra) — this changes the hosting line significantly

Emily — happy to be the escalation for any finance questions. If these concessions look reasonable I'll authorize the one-time credit and the refundability term.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Finance & GTM Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
